readerCopy.body: Questions of authority become harder to ignore when pressure to act meets a refusal to be managed. When Mars opposes Lilith, a disagreement can keep circling the details while the harder issue is who gets to decide and whose refusal is being treated as negotiable. If you catch yourself arguing the details, notice if the harder question is who actually gets a say. Compromise works only when everyone involved still has agency. Exhausting one side until it gives in may end the argument without creating agreement.
